static_traits.name: Lin Mei
static_traits.family_status: Married to wife, Has two children; wife generally supportive, but the relationship is somewhat affected by his self-blame over 'insufficient provision'
static_traits.social_status: Main Social support comes from the wife, but he tends to internalize stress, struggling to reveal vulnerability to his wife; other social networks Not mentioned
static_traits.medical_history: Without major physical illness; without similar prior psychological problems or treatment history
static_traits.language_features: High cooperation, clear expression, Good logic; able to self-reflect but markedly self-critical; initially slightly tense, overall restrained and serious tone

basic_info.main_problem: I constantly feel my provision for the family is not enough, although I work hard as a Truck driver; this sense of inadequacy appeared when finances became stressful several years ago, and worsened when seeing other families vacationing and camping.
basic_info.core_demands: The persistent feeling of 'not being good enough for the family' has affected physical and mental health; I hope to address these thoughts and emotions in therapy.
growth_experiences: After family financial pressure rose several years ago, started feeling inferiority and Anxiety about 'insufficient provision', believing one's worth is highly tied to whether the family can live 'the best life'.

Unable to afford a family vacation this summer, self-blame and sense of failure intensified significantly after seeing other families' travel photos on social media, then 'compensated' by extending work hours and taking extra deliveries.

Every night after work repeatedly reflecting on whether 'enough is provided', Low mood affecting sleep and Work performance; the relationship with his wife became tense because of this, and although his wife expresses gratitude and support, he still struggles to open up to her to avoid worrying her.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough/not capable enough
One's value as a partner and parent depends on financial provision and tangible experiences (such as holidays, camping)

special_situations.event: Seeing photos on social media of other families going out on vacation or camping
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot provide vacations/more activities for the family, it means I have failed, I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Compensating and proving oneself by working overtime and taking more deliveries
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am letting my family down/I am not as good as others

special_situations.event: After Working long hours, reflecting at the end of the day on 'whether I provide enough'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I still feel it is not enough, then that is the fact, I am indeed not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pressures himself and keeps extending work hours to be 'enough'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter how hard I try it is not enough

special_situations.event: Unable to arrange a family vacation this summer due to budget constraints
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot even afford one vacation, it means I am making my family suffer, I have failed as a provider
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately looking for more shifts and extra deliveries to 'make up for it'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is It is all my fault, I let them down

special_situations.event: When realizing one can already stably support the family, still evaluating oneself by the standard of 'not enough yet'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only doing more and giving more counts as competent; existing efforts and achievements do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating existing achievements, continuously raising standards and working overtime
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: What I am doing now is still not enough

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be a reliable and affirmed provider, making the family happy and gaining unconditional recognition
core_conflict.fear: Fears making family suffer, being seen as a failure, and losing the partner's respect and intimacy
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of worth and control through self-pressure and overwork
Repressing vulnerability and needs to avoid worrying the wife, maintaining the 'strong one/provider' image

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough provider, easily One who disappoints the family
object_relations.object_representation: Family/partner who have expectations of me and will be disappointed if I do not give enough

object_relations.self_representation: A parent at a disadvantage in comparisons
object_relations.object_representation: An idealized and judgmental 'other families' (reference others on social media)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to express inner stress to the wife or talk about feelings of 'insufficient provision'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Expressing vulnerability will worry the wife, and also means I am incompetent, failing
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoids emotion words and expressions of need, tone is restrained, emphasizes the factual statement 'I will work harder', reducing pauses and self-exposure.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing others' vacations on social media or talking about being unable to afford a vacation this year
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others' vacations symbolize my incompetence, and signal I must do more to not be looked down upon
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using 'should/must' type statements to emphasize responsibility and provision, quickly shifting to overtime plans and goals, downplaying personal emotions and limits.

manifestations: Bound by the role expectation of 'must be a perfect provider', struggling to freely choose and prioritize between Work and family
Fighting Anxiety with overtime, sacrificing autonomy and rest
outcomes: Sleep impaired and Physical and mental exhaustion

manifestations: Unwilling to reveal unease to the wife to avoid worrying her, choosing to internalize stress
Feeling self-isolation and inadequacy in comparison
outcomes: Relationship tension and widening emotional distance
Increased negative rumination, Lowered sense of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Uses 'I should/must give more' as the only standard of self-evaluation
Treats external indicators such as 'whether one can go on vacation' as the yardstick of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When talking about feelings, quickly shifts to work plans and overtime arrangements, avoiding vulnerability and needs
Displacing focus from inner Anxiety onto actions and tasks

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Worries about burdening the wife, suppresses expression
High-frequency self-blame and negative rumination, hard to internalize positive feedback

positive_force: Stable job and a continuous sense of responsibility, willing to give for the family
Partner (wife) expresses gratitude and support, providing emotional resources
Having self-reflection and motivation to seek help, willing to try new methods
Already able to basically secure family life, with realistic providing ability
negative_force: Excessively binds self-worth to economic provision/visible activities (vacations), seeking external validation
Excessive comparison and negating positive evidence, emotional reasoning and black-and-white thinking
Repressing vulnerability, struggling to communicate needs, rigid role expectations ('should/must')
Long-term fatigue and Sleep impaired, further lowering emotional regulation and relationship quality

target_behavior.behavior: Extending work hours and frequent overtime to relieve Anxiety about 'insufficient provision'
antecedent: Sees others' family vacations/camping on social media
Reflecting after work on 'whether enough is provided'
When facing tight family budgets or being unable to arrange vacations
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief directly equating 'providing more' with 'personal worth', accompanied by cognitive biases of comparison and negating positive information
target_behavior.function: Escaping guilt and Anxiety, seeking a sense of control and external recognition
target_behavior.consequence: Physical and mental exhaustion, Sleep affected, less communication with wife, further declining Work performance and relationship quality

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent negative rumination and Self-denial (such as 'I am not good enough' 'no matter how hard I try it is not enough')
antecedent: Sees social comparison cues of others vacationing and camping
Feeling exhausted or during the self-reflection time before sleep
Talking about family spending and budget
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive patterns of emotional reasoning, overgeneralization and negating positive information maintain the 'failure' self-schema
target_behavior.function: Obtaining motivation to improve and an illusion of control through self-blame, while avoiding more complex realistic evaluation and communication
target_behavior.consequence: Worsening Anxiety and guilt, Declining sleep quality, Relationship tension with partner, impaired daytime attention and Work performance
